slides.0.title: Tank-method and aromatic sparkling wines
slides.0.subtitle: Fresh fruit is the point: the faster the better
slides.1.title: Prosecco
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Variety and style
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Based on Glera (at least 85%), with the tank method preserving pear, green apple and white-flower notes; light-bodied and usually drunk young
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Hierarchy
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Reorganised in 2009: above the broad Prosecco DOC sit two DOCGs, Conegliano Valdobbiadene and Asolo; within the DOCG are finer names such as Rive (single-village slopes) and Cartizze
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Prosecco Rosé
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Since 2020 the DOC allows rosé: Glera with 10–15% Pinot Nero, at least 60 days in tank, and it must carry a vintage
slides.1.content: The key Prosecco argument is the price and image gap between flatland volume DOC and steep-slope DOCG.
slides.2.title: Asti and Moscato d’Asti
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Variety and method
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Moscato Bianco from Piedmont; a single fermentation in a pressurised tank keeps the CO₂ and is stopped by chilling at the desired alcohol, preserving natural grape sweetness and musky aromas
slides.2.highlights.1.title: How they differ
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Asti is fully sparkling (spumante) with higher alcohol; Moscato d’Asti is semi-sparkling (frizzante), lower in alcohol (around 5%), sweeter and more delicate
slides.2.highlights.2.title: When to drink
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Aroma is the selling point and fades with time, so drink soon after bottling; this is the “freshness first” logic of the tank method
slides.2.content: The Asti method is the only major sparkling method with a single fermentation: good material for comparisons.
slides.3.title: German Sekt and Lambrusco
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Sekt
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Germany is a major sparkling-wine market; much Sekt is tank-made, often from imported base wine, and only Deutscher Sekt must use German grapes; Winzersekt is made by growers from their own grapes by the traditional method
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Lambrusco
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red semi-sparkling wine from Emilia-Romagna, mostly tank-made, from dry to off-dry; high acidity, fruit and light tannin, traditionally paired with local cured meats and cheese
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Strengths of the tank method
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Fast, cheap and fruit-preserving, it suits volume production and young drinking; extended lees contact in tank (such as Prosecco Rosé’s 60 days) can add a little texture
slides.3.content: Methods are not better or worse; they match style goals and cost.
